title: Graft and Transplant
statementMd:
Alice and Bob have a tree with 𝑛n vertices numbered from 11 to 𝑛n, and they want to play a game on this tree to determine the only winner. They decide to perform the following operation alternately, with Alice going first. In each operation, they can choose two adjacent vertices 𝑢u and 𝑣v, and make all the undirected edges connecting 𝑢u, except the one connecting 𝑢u and 𝑣v, reconnect to 𝑣v instead of 𝑢u. In short, each edge (𝑢,𝑤)(u,w) where 𝑤≠𝑣w≠v changes to (𝑣,𝑤)(v,w) after the operation.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0fc25c2ab77cf5f68e369b0ed0d31e40ff3e2b11.png) Figure: The "Graft and Transplant" Operation

However, they soon realize that such an operation will probably result in a game that never ends, so they add an extra rule that the two trees before and after an operation must not be isomorphic. More formally, let 𝑉(𝑆)V(S) be the set of vertices in a tree 𝑆S and 𝑉(𝑇)V(T) be the set of vertices in a tree 𝑇T. Tree 𝑆S and tree 𝑇T are *isomorphic* if there exists a bijection 𝑓:𝑉(𝑆)→𝑉(𝑇)f:V(S)→V(T) such that for all pairs of vertices (𝑢,𝑣)(u,v) in 𝑉(𝑆)V(S), 𝑢u and 𝑣v are connected by an edge in 𝑆S if and only if vertices 𝑓(𝑢)f(u) and 𝑓(𝑣)f(v) are connected by an edge in 𝑇T. Namely, 𝑓(𝑠)=𝑡f(s)=t implies vertex 𝑠s in 𝑆S corresponds to vertex 𝑡t in 𝑇T.

In this scenario, when one player cannot perform any valid operations, the other player will win the game. Assuming both Alice and Bob are clever enough and will adopt the best strategy to win or prevent the opponent from winning if one is unable to win, you need to predict the winner.

## Input

The first line contains an integer 𝑛n (2≤𝑛≤502≤n≤50), denoting the number of vertices in the tree.

Then 𝑛−1n−1 lines follow, each of which contains two integers 𝑢u and 𝑣v (1≤𝑢,𝑣≤𝑛)1≤u,v≤n), denoting an undirected edge connecting vertices 𝑢u and 𝑣v. It is guaranteed that the given edges form a tree.

## Output

Output "`Alice`" if Alice will win the game, "`Bob`" if Bob will win the game, or "`Draw`" if the game under the extra rule will still never end if both of them perform their operations optimally.
